rules.title: An application is blocking the feature update
rules.explanation: Windows Setup or SetupDiag reported an actionable application compatibility block.
rules.recommendation: Identify the named application or residual file in the evidence, update or remove it through the vendor-supported process, then repeat the compatibility scan.

rules.title: The device does not satisfy Setup requirements
rules.explanation: Windows Setup returned the system-requirements compatibility block.
rules.recommendation: Review TPM, Secure Boot, CPU, memory, storage, boot mode, and the compatibility XML before retrying.

rules.title: Windows Setup reported insufficient installation space
rules.explanation: The compatibility scan or SetupDiag reported that the OS or system partition lacks required free space.
rules.recommendation: Review the partition table and free-space evidence. Free space using an approved process; do not alter EFI or recovery partitions without a separate change plan.

rules.title: Setup encountered a driver-associated rollback
rules.explanation: The 0xC1900101 family normally requires correlation with the extend code, SetupAPI, crash, and device evidence to identify the responsible driver.
rules.recommendation: Use the phase, operation, named device, SetupAPI excerpt, and dump evidence in this report to update, remove, or isolate the specific driver through its vendor-supported process.

rules.title: The requested application-and-data migration choice is unavailable
rules.explanation: Windows Setup reported that the selected migration choice cannot be used with the supplied image, edition, language, or installation state.
rules.recommendation: Confirm that target media matches the installed architecture, edition, and system default UI language, then review the named compatibility evidence before retrying.

rules.title: Windows Setup could not select a matching installation image
rules.explanation: The media did not provide a unique applicable image for the current edition, language, architecture, and licensing state.
rules.recommendation: Use organization-approved media matching the installed architecture, edition, and system default UI language; do not force an unrelated image index.

rules.title: A previous installation requires cleanup or restart
rules.explanation: Windows Setup reported unfinished cleanup from an earlier attempt.
rules.recommendation: Complete the pending restart and verify that no upgrade is still active. Preserve logs before using any approved cache-cleanup procedure.
patterns: cleanup operation from a previous installation

rules.title: Windows Setup required explicit EULA acceptance
rules.explanation: A quiet Windows 11 Setup operation was invoked without the required EULA acceptance option.
rules.recommendation: Correct the deployment command after confirming organizational licensing and acceptance requirements.

rules.title: Failure occurred during SafeOS boot preparation
rules.explanation: The extend code points to a SafeOS boot failure, commonly associated with storage, firmware, boot configuration, encryption, or boot-critical drivers.
rules.recommendation: Correlate this code with boot-critical drivers, BCD, BitLocker, storage health, and setup dump evidence in the report.

rules.title: A device installation operation failed
rules.explanation: The extend code or SetupDiag result identifies device/driver installation during first boot.
rules.recommendation: Review SetupAPI, problem devices, recent third-party drivers, and the matching timestamp before changing any driver.

rules.title: Setup aborted while migrating data or settings
rules.explanation: The migration engine reported an explicit abort or abandoned an object after an error.
rules.recommendation: Use the affected file, registry key, profile, or application named in the evidence. Validate its health and permissions through an approved remediation before retrying.

rules.title: Component-store or package corruption was detected
rules.explanation: DISM, CBS, or Windows Update reported a corruption or missing-source error that can prevent feature-update servicing.
rules.recommendation: Review the exact CBS/DISM package and source evidence. Plan component repair separately; this diagnostic tool intentionally does not perform it.

rules.title: Servicing could not update a boot or reserved partition
rules.explanation: The 0x800F0922 family can indicate reserved-partition capacity, connectivity, or servicing-finalization problems.
rules.recommendation: Correlate partition, network, CBS, and DISM evidence before choosing a remediation; the code alone is not specific enough.

rules.title: SFC verify-only found protected-file integrity violations
rules.explanation: The read-only SFC verification reported protected Windows resource integrity violations. The diagnostic tool did not repair them.
rules.recommendation: Review the SFC and CBS evidence and use the organization's approved servicing-repair workflow outside this diagnostic tool before another feature-update attempt.
patterns: Windows Resource Protection found integrity violations
Windows Resource Protection found corrupt files

rules.title: DISM failed while servicing the upgrade image
rules.explanation: SetupDiag identified a DISM image-session or provider failure.
rules.recommendation: Use the SetupDiag message, phase, operation, and DISM log excerpt to determine whether source files, servicing state, or a provider failed.

rules.title: A bug check occurred during the upgrade window
rules.explanation: Setup, WER, or the System event log recorded a kernel bug check. Unless SetupDiag or a setup-specific dump links it to the attempt, this remains a low-confidence temporal association.
rules.recommendation: Analyze setupmem.dmp or the matching minidump with approved debugging tools and correlate the blamed module with the driver inventory.

rules.title: Storage or file-system errors occurred near setup
rules.explanation: Setup or system evidence contains corruption, I/O, NTFS, disk, or controller errors. The finding remains low confidence until the device, timestamp, or operation correlates it to the upgrade attempt.
rules.recommendation: Review the named volume/device and storage-health evidence. Perform any repair or hardware action under a separate approved procedure.

rules.title: A compatibility safeguard hold is active
rules.explanation: Windows compatibility intelligence indicates that this device is gated from the target release.
rules.recommendation: Use the safeguard ID in the report to review Windows release health. Do not bypass the hold unless your organization has separately approved and validated that risk.

rules.title: Windows Update encountered a proxy, DNS, or source-connectivity failure
rules.explanation: Windows Update or BITS recorded a name-resolution, proxy-authentication, timeout, or connection failure while contacting an update source.
rules.recommendation: Correlate the timestamp and endpoint with WinHTTP proxy, DNS, routes, time, WSUS policy, and connectivity results; change network policy only through the owning team.

rules.title: Windows Update encountered a TLS, certificate, content-decoding, or clock failure
rules.explanation: The update transport recorded a secure-channel error commonly associated with TLS inspection/configuration, certificate trust, content decoding, or an incorrect clock.
rules.recommendation: Use the captured time-service, proxy, certificate-related event, and update-log evidence to identify the responsible boundary before retrying.

rules.title: Windows Update failed an offer, download, or installation operation
rules.explanation: Windows Update or BITS recorded a failure affecting all updates, downloaded content, or update installation orchestration.
rules.recommendation: Identify the update ID and timestamp in WindowsUpdate.log and event evidence, then correlate servicing, security-agent, storage, and source-ownership signals.

rules.title: SetupDiag reported a BitLocker compatibility block
rules.explanation: The target or current encryption configuration prevented Setup from proceeding.
rules.recommendation: Review BitLocker state and any third-party encryption filter drivers. Never expose recovery passwords in the diagnostic package.

rules.title: The current boot state does not support an in-place upgrade
rules.explanation: SetupDiag reported Safe Mode, Audit Mode, Windows To Go, or VHD boot as a hard block.
rules.recommendation: Return the device to a supported normal boot state through an approved procedure before retrying.

rules.title: Windows Setup recorded a fatal error
rules.explanation: A fatal or explicit rollback entry was found but requires its adjacent evidence to identify the responsible component.
rules.recommendation: Start with the last fatal entry for this attempt and follow its code, phase, operation, and correlated evidence shown in the report.
